CHAPTER ONE

Uchechi, God’s will

Your name means God’s will. Not God’s maybe. Not God’s “let’s see.” God’s will.

Before anyone called you Mommy, the heavens had already written a plan with your name on it. And nne, that plan was never small.

CHAPTER TWO

The day everything changed

“Not us looking like twins!” 😂

Look at that tiny face next to yours. Same smile, same eyes, same trouble waiting to happen.

That day a little boy chose you, and you became his whole world. That is when dike nwanyi (warrior woman) was born.

CHAPTER THREE

The nights nobody clapped

Nobody gave you an award for the 3am fevers. Or the prayers you whispered when the house was quiet.

Or for being mommy, daddy, driver, chef, nurse and referee in one body. Or for saying “I’m fine” on days you were not.

You carried it alone, and you carried it gracefully. Nobody clapped, but heaven kept every receipt. 🤍

Still glowing through it all ✨
CHAPTER FOUR

He saw all of it

You may think the little one wasn’t watching. Oh, he was. Every sacrifice. Every prayer. Every time you chose him.

His handwriting. His heart.
“I hear you pray for me every day and it really warms my heart.”
“Twinzie” 🥹
“I’m so happy to be your son.”

Read that again, Uckoko. Your child, with his own hands, wrote that you did it right. 😭

CHAPTER FIVE

Level 12 unlocked 🎮

“Almost my height!! God abeg 🥹”

When did he grow?! One minute he’s in a checkered shirt, now he’s taller than your excuses.

The two of you. Always.
Laughing together, because that’s what you two do.
The rise of the shining generation 🙏

A boy standing tall with a microphone, unafraid. Where do you think that confidence came from? From you, nne.

CHAPTER SIX

And still… yupiee? 😂

Hold on. Let me get this straight.

Single mother. Full-time hustle. Prayer warrior. Chief of homework. And you still show up looking like that?!

Nwanyi oma! Ezenwanyi! Ada di egwu! Who gave you permission to be this beautiful AND this strong? Give some to the rest of us na! 😂

The skin is glowing. The slay is slaying. Even tired, you carry grace like it was made for you. Because it was.

Exhibit A: a masterpiece standing in front of masterpieces 🖼️
Exhibit B: pink dress, blue sky, zero stress.
Exhibit C: serving looks like it’s her job 💅
Exhibit D: four poses, one parking lot, no mercy 😂
Exhibit E: and these faces! Pure chaos 😂
Exhibit F: the bob that ended arguments.
CHAPTER SEVEN

What I need you to know

You are beautiful. And I don’t mean only the face. I mean the way you love, the way you keep going, and the way you pray for people who forget to pray for you.

You are resilient. Life tested you and you came out softer, wiser, and more radiant. You did not just survive motherhood. You did it beautifully.

This face. This heart. This woman. 🤍

On the hard days, remember that a young man is cheering for you louder than anyone. And so am I. Always. 🤍

CHAPTER EIGHT

Give thanks

Your birthday hasn’t arrived yet, and that is part of the gift. From today until your day, I want you to sit with these memories and say thank you.

Thank you for the boy who is growing tall. For the strength you didn’t know you had. For every prayer God answered, even the ones that came in disguise. For the years behind you and the ones still waiting.

Come back and read this whenever you need to remember who you are. Gratitude looks good on you, nne. Almost as good as that pink dress. 😂
